articles.title: Conspiratorial Canadian search engine class action lawsuit against Apple going forward
articles.content: A lawsuit alleges that a conspiratorial deal made between Apple and Google in 2005 locked competitive search engines out of the market, and a judge has inexplicably chosen to let it move to trial. Another lawsuit suggests Apple and Google are conspirators There are a lot of reasons to look at Apple and Google's relationship from a regulatory lens , but a new class action lawsuit in Canada takes a very peculiar angle. It isn't the first time Apple and Google's relationship has been brought into question , but the new class action lawsuit focuses on Apple. According to a filing in British Columbia first shared by 9to5Mac , a judge has chosen to allow a class action lawsuit against Apple to move forward to trial. It originally involved Google, but Google Search Ads has an arbitration clause that had to be honored. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.title: Cisco to link all future products to its SaaS-y Cloud Control management tool
articles.content: Cisco will no longer create products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control, its SaaS-y management platform that offers netadmins a single tool to manage all of the networking giant’s devices and much of its software portfolio. The networking giant announced Cloud Control in June 2025 and only made it available to customers in the USA. Cisco has previously told The Register that slow rollout reflects the fact that Cisco needs to nail privacy and other regulatory niceties, and deploy infrastructure, before introducing the service to other markets. It appears Cisco is now satisfied it has sorted out those issues. Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing, today told the company’s Live conference in Australia that Cloud Control will come online in the European Union, UK, and Down Under in February 2027. Japan, India, and Canada will get their turn in May. Schultz said Cisco is “working tirelessly” to deploy Cloud Control across the world as soon as possible. He also revealed that, starting next year, Cisco will no longer ship products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control. That doesn’t mean those products will be manageable only if they can connect to Cloud Control. Instead, the decision reflects Cisco’s belief that the main thing stopping its customers buying more of its products is the complexity of operating them in concert. Schultz also feels that Cloud Control represents “platform advantage” for Cisco, because when users integrate networking, security, and observability the result is better manageability and resilience. Schultz also told the conference that Cisco will bundle its Thousand Eyes observability and security tool with the “Essentials” and “Advantage” licenses. “We admit it was hard to license and deploy,” he said during his keynote speech, adding that the tool will be deployed automatically with Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 hardware. Another product Cisco plans to bring to more customers is Live Protect, a tool that implements compensating controls for flaws that organizations can’t immediately patch. The product has become particularly useful since Anthropic's Mythos model, and similar AI offerings, made it possible to quickly find more software bugs and flaws and overwhelmed tech teams whose patching apparatus was not set up to handle hundreds of montly CVEs. Live Protect currently works on some of Cisco's datacenter switches, plus SD-WAN and WLAN controllers. From December, Cisco will extend it to 8000 series routers, secure firewalls, campus gateway, and to Cloud Control itself. From May 2027, Live Protect will work with Cisco’s ASR 9000 series service aggregation routers and Network Convergence System. "Expect this to be a major investment area," Schultz added. ®

articles.title: FDA Warns GLP-1s May Increase Risk of Sudden Blindness
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from NBC News: The Food and Drug Administration said Monday that GLP-1 drugmakers must add a warning label about a rare eye condition that can cause sudden blindness. The condition, called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, or NAION, affects the optic nerve, which carries signals from the eye to the brain. When blood flow to the nerve is reduced or blocked, it can cause sudden vision loss. The condition is permanent with no known treatment. The FDA said "there is a potential increased risk of rare NAION" in people taking GLP-1 drugs. The agency's requirement applies to all GLP-1s, including Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Wegovy and Eli Lilly's Mounjaro and Zepbound, as well as several older GLP-1 diabetes medications. [...] Previous research has found that GLP-1 use may increase the risk of NAION, and Lilly has said it was aware of studies on the potential link. The FDA said it began looking into a possible link after a 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology that found diabetes patients prescribed semaglutide were four times as likely to develop NAION as those not prescribed the drug. The agency said it reviewed reports of side effects submitted to its adverse event monitoring system and analyzed data from multiple clinical trials. Cases of NAION have been reported for all currently marketed GLP-1 drugs, the FDA found. However, FDA scientists were not able to identify a mechanism for how the drugs could increase the risk of the eye condition. Risk factors for NAION can overlap with conditions seen in people taking GLP-1 drugs, including Type 2 diabetes, obesity, sleep apnea and hypertension. "Patients and caregivers should be aware of a potential increased risk of NAION, a rare condition that can result in acute, painless, decreased vision in one eye, including permanent vision loss," with GLP-1 use, the FDA said in the release. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Microsoft’s email security is unexpectedly blocking legitimate business mail
articles.content: Microsoft’s email filters meant to protect users from malicious messages appear to be rejecting legitimate ones. Over the last few days, some mail sent to Microsoft consumer addresses have bounced if they did not publish a domain-based message authentication, reporting, and conformance (DMARC) record. This includes messages to Outlook, Hotmail, Live, and MSN. The refusals began November 5 and are ongoing as of publication time . Microsoft did not announce a policy change and has not published a postmaster notice, service-health entry, or other blog post. The issue may indicate that a policy change and a bug may both be in play, noted Frank Dickson of Dickson Research. “Requiring every sending domain to prove it is who it says it is makes email safer,” he pointed out. “Doing it without notice, with an error message that points at the wrong problem, makes a mess.” Intermittent sending issues DMARC is meant to protect against spoofing, phishing , and business email compromise. Microsoft has had a rule in place since May 2025 requiring DMARC, but only from domains sending more than 5,000 messages a day to consumer mailboxes. But as of November 5, mail from small, ordinary senders, rather than from bulk ones, have been bounced due to lack of DMARC, Sender Policy Framework (SPF), or DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM). Senders have been receiving Non-Delivery Reports (NDRs) citing 550 5.7.1 or 550 5.7.23 errors, but are doing so inconsistently; some messages are getting through while others are rejected. For instance, one user reported this error message on Microsoft’s community forum : Your message to @hotmail.com couldn’t be delivered. hotmail.com couldn’t confirm that your message was sent from a trusted location. Another user reported the same problem, adding: “Some emails work fine and others return errors with SPF failed.” Adding to the confusion, some bounced domains were reported to have working SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. A Microsoft external staff moderator called it a “service degradation” currently under active investigation. According to email security company MailRoute , enterprises can determine if their domain is impacted with this command on any terminal (replacing example.com with their domain): dig +short TXT _dmarc.example.com . A response starting with v=DMARC1 means there is a DMARC record; no reply means there isn’t, MailRoute said. The fix is a single TXT record: v=DMARC1 ; p=none . This declares that a domain uses DMARC and asks receivers to send reports, but it tells them to take no action on failures, MailRoute explained. DMARC meant to make impersonation difficult DMARC relies on two foundational email authentication tools that must be active on a domain: SPF and DKIM. SPF verifies whether the sending server’s IP address is allowed to send email on behalf of a domain, while DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to the message to prove it wasn’t altered along the way and actually belongs to the domain it says it is coming from. DMARC checks the two, identifying whether the domain listed on the “from” address aligns with the validated domains. It ties those checks to the name the reader actually sees and tells receivers what to do with forgeries, Dickson explained. “Without it, impersonating your domain is easy,” he said. “That is where a lot of phishing and business email compromise starts.” But because Microsoft, at least to this point, has only required DMARC for larger senders, it is not standard across the board; many small senders reasonably concluded it did not apply to them, Dickson noted. This includes SMBs, nonprofits, schools, and professional practices such as law firms, accountants, and doctors’ offices running on domains that “someone set up years ago, and nobody has touched since.” Larger organizations miss DMARC on secondary domains, regional domains, and the subdomains that their marketing and billing platforms send from for mundane reasons. articles.title: How skills and agents work in AWS Quick
articles.content: If you use AI agents, you’ve probably explained the same task more than once. You might describe how to build your weekly status update, write release notes, manage a project, or create tickets. These are all repeatable tasks that you can encode using AWS Quick through agents and skills. AWS Quick is an AI-powered service for automating tasks, analyzing data, building web applications, and conducting research. You work with it in natural language, and Quick uses AI agents to process your requests against your connected data sources and applications. In this post, we cover how agents, skills, and your data fit together in AWS Quick, and how to build and share skills that work for your team. We also show how the official catalog and custom agents help you put those skills to use. Understanding foundational concepts In this section, we explain the foundational concepts that help you understand AWS Quick in relation to agents, skills, and your data. Figure 1: How a Quick agent follows its instructions, loads the skills a task needs, acts through connectors, and grounds its answers in your data The agent sits at the center of Figure 1. It follows its instructions, loads the skills that a task calls for, takes action through connectors, and grounds its answers in your data: spaces, knowledge bases, datasets, and dashboards. Working with agents An agent in AWS Quick is a configurable AI with its own instructions, knowledge sources (spaces), and connectors, which it uses to answer questions and get work done for you. You can work with an agent in chat, or let it run on its own using a routine . Agents can only reach the resources and services that you can, and you decide what each agent is allowed to do. Quick is the default built-in agent that every user has access to. It has no fixed scope, so in each conversation it works with whatever resources you have access to, such as your spaces, knowledge bases, dashboards, connectors, and skills. You don’t need to decide in advance which data or tools a request needs, so you can start most work with Quick. A custom agent is one that you or someone on your team configures for a specific job. An example is a human resources (HR) onboarding assistant that answers new-hire questions from the HR team’s space. You give it its own instructions and limit it to the spaces, connectors, and skills that your use case requires. After you test and publish it, you can share it with other users and groups within your AWS Quick account. For a walkthrough of building one, see Build AI-powered employee onboarding agents with AWS Quick . Working with data Agents ground their answers in the data you connect to Quick. A space is a curated collection of documents and AWS Quick resources that an agent uses as a source of information. You can create one for yourself, your team, or another group in your organization. You can upload files and folders to a space, or add assets such as dashboards, knowledge bases, action connectors, and datasets. When you start a conversation with Quick, you can attach a space to narrow the data that Quick uses for that conversation. When you add a space to an agent, the space becomes part of the agent’s configuration, and the agent draws on it when a request needs it. A knowledge base is an organized, indexed collection of documents or content from data sources, optimized for retrieval and question answering. Quick syncs knowledge bases from sources such as Google Drive, Microsoft OneDrive, Confluence, Microsoft SharePoint, Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), web crawler, or Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Bases . Quick keeps them up to date on a sync schedule. Datasets and dashboards come from AWS Quick Sight , the business intelligence feature in Quick, which is available in accounts provisioned through the AWS Management Console. A dataset is a prepared collection of data ready for use in analyses and dashboards. A dashboard is the published version of an analysis that you…

articles.title: Law firm files class-action lawsuit against Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang confirms affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.content: The baying of the hounds can be heard at a distance. Yesterday, Nvidia's Jensen Huang confirmed that it was indeed true that he had a romantic affair with Alice Huang (not related to the family), who U.S. intelligence services claim is a Chinese honeypot tasked with facilitating smuggling of the firm's advanced GPUs into China. Now, a class-action lawsuit and investigations have started flying from almost everywhere. This development is not unexpected, as basic securities law allows shareholders to sue their investees if they misrepresent facts or otherwise perform actions that cause a drop in stock prices. They may have a point, as Nvidia's shares dipped significantly when the confirmation of Jensen's infidelity and the ramifications thereof hit the press everywhere. The legal proceedings are bound to be numerous, but as of right now, the first class-action lawsuit was filed by the Rosen Law Firm. The suit claims that Nvidia and Jensen Huang failed to disclose or misled investors regarding Jensen's affair with Alice, lied about it when asked, raised national security concerns, and caused a subsequent loss of Nvidia's reputation. You can check out the case docket at PacerMonitor here . While legal analysis is beyond the scope of this news, Nvidia did downplay Jensen's relationship with Alice, saying that "Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year." Other legal firms have launched their own investigations into the recent development, with essentially the same justification: Schall, Brown & Schwartz attributes a 5.5% pre-market-trading drop to Nvidia, as does Levi & Korsinsky . The office of Frank R. Cruz mentions an 8.8% figure related to intra-day exchanging, and is interested in shareholders with $50,000 in losses. The percentage-drop figure is 5.88% premarket for Bronstein, Gewritz & Grossman . Every investigation and suit mentioned here requires no upfront fees from complainants, as with most class-action lawsuits. The underlying condition is often that the law firms involved get a cut of whichever damages or settlements may appear at the end of the lawsuit. Some of them, like the one by Levi & Korsinsky, even aim to relieve investors who've already sold their Nvidia shares and sold them at a loss, with no minimum amount required.

articles.title: Anthropic's super bug-finding Mythos model is going into Cisco and IBM products
articles.content: Anthropic has started extending access to its bug-finding Mythos model by allowing Cisco and IBM to make it part of their security products. Cisco announced its integration today at an event in Melbourne, Australia, where it revealed that the red teaming tools in its AI Defense suite, which looks for weaknesses and inappropriate activity in AI models, agents, and applications they power, will be able to call Mythos to test customers’ setups. “At a very high level, AI Defense has the ability to look at models and break them,” said Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing. He said the tool is now “super-charged by Mythos” and will identify more danger that AI Defense will then address. AI Defense already uses AI-powered red teaming to find flaws. Mythos will become another option. Cisco will make it available under users’ existing licenses, without additional cost. Natalie Mead, Anthropic’s head of applied AI for the Asia-Pacific, said the company has a long queue of buyers who want to use Mythos, and working with Cisco will make it easier to satisfy that demand. Anthropic initially made Mythos available under "Project Glasswing," a program that gave vetted organizations access to the model to test their codebases, but has since expanded access through other controlled programs, an arrangement that makes considerable sense because in the wrong hands Mythos could help attackers exploit software flaws. The Cisco deal exposes the functionality of Mythos to end-users, without letting them use the model itself. The Register asked Mead if Anthropic has similar deals with other third parties and she demurred. That may be because a few hours after Cisco told us about its use of Mythos, IBM announced that it will also integrate Anthropic’s model into a product – namely its Concert tool, which uses AI to scan applications for risks and weaknesses. IBM says it will use Mythos “to uncover weaknesses traditional scanners miss, determine which pose real risk and generate fixes for developer approval.” We have asked Anthropic if these integrations represent a decision to open Mythos to more users in more ways. We will update this story if we receive a substantial response. Also on Monday, Anthropic introduced version 5.2 of Mythos and Fable, which the company says generate outputs up to 30 percent faster than version 5.1 yet cost less: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Users can choose to run both models in “fast mode,” which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times, and doubles prices to $16 per million input tokens and $80 per million output tokens. Anthropic says it “ran extensive prerelease safety testing on the model that underlies Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. This included developing novel evaluations that give deeper insight into specific concerning behaviors like sandbox escapes.” After those tests, the company concluded “high-stakes risks from misalignment remain low, and the model performed as well as, or better than, our recent models on most alignment measures. “Fable 5.2’s cyber and biology safeguards are as robust as those of Fable 5.1 but produce fewer unnecessary blocks, and we have implemented our strongest-ever protections against distillation attacks.” The latter is a telling admission, given Anthropic believes Chinese AI labs use distillation to effectively clone its models without doing expensive training work. ®

articles.title: Microsoft Took 31 Years to Let You Kill Windows 11's Sticky Keys Popup
articles.content: Microsoft is testing a Windows 11 option that lets users permanently disable the Sticky Keys and Filter Keys activation prompts directly from the pop-ups themselves, ending a 31-year-old annoyance without requiring a trip into Settings. Windows Latest reports: Sadly, the dialog is still the same aging Win32 window, but we spotted Microsoft's design boss replying under an X post reply about this, saying he is working on modernizing legacy dialogs. The popup might be annoying, but did you know that it exists because of a pinball game from 1995? [...] The change is in Build 26340.9882 (Experimental) and Build 26320.9876 (Beta), both released on November 6 and based on Windows 11 version 26H2. Microsoft says you can "choose not to be asked again" from the Sticky Keys and Filter Keys dialogs, but it's a Controlled Feature Rollout in Experimental, so you may not see it yet. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Here's What Apple Fixed in iOS 27.2.1 and macOS 27.2.1
articles.content: The iOS 27.2.1 , iPadOS 27.2.1, and macOS 27.2.1 updates Apple released today fix a handful of security vulnerabilities. With the security fixes implemented, it's a good idea to update as soon as you can. A bug with iMessage could let a remote attacker join a group chat to receive its messages, and another could let users see messages sent before they joined a group chat. Most of the vulnerabilities involved AirPlay and Bluetooth. A malicious Bluetooth device could pair without user interaction, and another bug could let a nearby attacker corrupt process memory. Several bugs could allow an attacker to bypass the rate limit on ‌AirPlay‌ pairing code attempts. Apple credits itself on four of the vulnerabilities, so they were found internally. With the macOS update, Apple also addressed the eMudhra certificate vulnerability , adding protections for command-line tools. Apple did not say that the flaws have been exploited in the wild, but with the details on each vulnerability now public, devices that are not running the new software could be more vulnerable to attack. articles.title: A $60 billion fintech hired a 14-year-old. Its CEO explains why.
articles.content: Ramp hired a 14-year-old intern after discovering an app he had built for fun that attracted attention from roughly a million people on Twitter. Co-CEO Eric Glyman discussed the hire during a November 5 interview with founder and editor of Upstairs Media, Alex Konrad , explaining how the $60 billion fintech company evaluates engineering talent beyond traditional qualifications, a recalibration playing out across the industry as AI redraws what a junior role even means . A viral app, no assignment “We had an intern who was 14 years old,” Glyman said. “Part of how we found him was he had built his own app for fun that was genuinely useful, and a million people saw it on Twitter and interacted with it. There was no one who was telling him, ‘Hey, go build this project.’ He just was interested in it.” Glyman did not identify the teenager or specify when he worked at Ramp. “Part of how we found him was he had built his own app for fun that was genuinely useful, and a million people saw it on Twitter…” The Minecraft server test Glyman says Ramp looks for developers who have pursued projects on their own, even when that experience doesn’t come from a conventional job, a premium on self-direction that grows sharper as AI erodes the entry-level tasks that once trained new engineers . “A lot of what we’re looking for is strong evidence that someone has built something on their own, created something on their own, and shown their drive where it didn’t come from other people saying, ‘I need you to go do something’.” “A lot of what we’re looking for is strong evidence that someone has built something on their own… and shown their drive where it didn’t come from other people saying, ‘I need you to go do something’.” In a separate November 3 interview with Blackstone , Glyman said Ramp also looks for developers who got their start running Minecraft servers as teenagers. Some teens built their own servers before high school, gaining practical programming experience long before entering the workforce. Glyman acknowledged that the approach has limits, since talented candidates who haven’t had the time, resources, or opportunity to build something independently could be overlooked at precisely the moment the entry-level rungs of the industry are already thinning out . A 28-year-old running engineering In June, Ramp appointed Rahul Sengottuvelu as chief technology officer at 28, replacing co-founder Karim Atiyeh , who became co-CEO alongside Glyman. Sengottuvelu joined Ramp through a 2023 acquisition and later led its applied AI team. He was already building AI products before ChatGPT became a household name. In its leadership announcement , Ramp pointed to Sengottuvelu’s experience building AI products and his ability to make tough technical decisions. He took over as CTO as the company was putting AI to work in more of its products and day-to-day operations. Small teams own the call Glyman also described how Ramp organizes its engineers into small teams of five or six people, giving them responsibility for deciding how to complete their projects. “If you look really deep into Ramp’s organizational design, it’s tons of small teams where we say, ‘Here’s the outcome we want you to drive, but it’s up to you.’ You can make the call on how you want to spend your time. Why hire someone who can surprise you with their creativity and then tell them, ‘Don’t make your own recipe’?” “Why hire someone who can surprise you with their creativity and then tell them, ‘Don’t make your own recipe’?” Glyman says adding more engineers doesn’t always mean getting work done faster since bigger teams often mean more people weighing in on decisions, which can add churn and slow workflow. articles.title: Everything we know so far about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting CEO Jensen Huang
articles.content: The leather-jacketed CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, has acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, spurring an investigation by his company and intense discussions worldwide. Recent reporting noted that since last year, US intelligence reports had identified Alice Huang (no relation) as not only the exec for an AI compute company renting access to Nvidia GPUs, but also a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies, including the “neoclouds” like Coreweave who have been some of its biggest customers. So far, Nvidia and Jensen Huang have said that they have “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised,” but that hasn’t settled things as the investigation continues. articles.title: Meta's Muse AI now has an Apple Watch app, which you shouldn't install
articles.content: Meta's AI agent has made its way to the Apple Watch , but all potential benefits are outweighed by the inherent risk associated with the tool, not to mention the privacy implications. Muse AI is available on the Apple Watch, but don't bother with it. Following its expansion to the iPad in October 2026 , Meta's Muse has received an Apple Watch companion app. The change was disclosed via the App Store page for Muse, which details the changes in version 15.0 of the iOS app. "Add Muse to your wrist with the new Apple Watch Companion app," reads the description. On the Apple Watch, users can now call and talk to Meta's virtual assistant, text it, or use dictation with Muse. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.title: Trump Backs Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Amid Chinese Spy Affair Investigation
articles.content: President Donald Trump says the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman alleged by U.S. intelligence to have gathered information for Beijing. "I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape," Trump said at a White House briefing. The Associated Press reports: Trump suggested the extraordinary step of directly involving himself in a counterintelligence investigation, a sign of his friendly relationship with Huang and the possible geopolitical stakes. "I did speak to him today just to see if he's feeling all right, how you're doing," Trump said. "He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy." Trump is slated to meet next week with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, but he was noncommittal about bringing up the situation with Xi. "No, I don't think so," Trump said. "I mean, maybe. I'm sure President XI will ask me about it. I just know Jensen very well. I just think he's a very honorable man." Nvidia has launched its own independent investigation into whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Meanwhile, China has denied the allegations. "The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said during a regular news briefing Monday. Further reading: Commerce Dept. Chip Inquiry Was Halted After Nvidia Intervention Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: France blames Iran for supermarket hack meltdowns
articles.content: France has turned up the heat on Iran over destructive cyberattacks targeting refrigeration controllers at more than 700 grocery stores in October, spoiling food and sparking fires. The country vowed to take action using “all available means of response.” The supermarket attacks , which affected Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché groups, started at least 15 fires and caused food losses in the tens of millions of euros, according to a Monday report by France’s Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre (C4). The C4 includes the National Cybersecurity Agency of France, the Directorate General for External Security, the Directorate General for Internal Security, the Directorate General for Armament, and the Cyber Defence Command. “This is an unprecedented campaign in terms of its scale and level of aggressiveness, thus constituting the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory,” France’s Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs said in a statement . All signs point to CyberAv3ngers Both the report and the statement attributed the refrigeration controller hacks to the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ (IRGC) Shahid Kaveh cyber unit. The Shahid Kaveh unit, which French national security officials say is led by Reza Salarvand and Mahdi Lashgarian, is better known by its hacktivist personas, including CyberAv3ngers . This is the same crew suspected of involvement in the July attacks that targeted more than 100 internet-exposed water systems in America. While the US government hasn’t attributed the intrusions to any country or group, private-sector security analysts blamed Iran , and specifically CyberAv3ngers . The IRGC-affiliated hacking crew has been breaking into industrial controllers for years , and in 2023, American national security and law enforcement agencies attributed a series of cyberattacks against "multiple" US water facilities to CyberAv3ngers. “The Iranian cyber threat against French interests is not new,” according to the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. “Iran has already carried out several destabilizing acts against us, notably targeting the weekly magazine Charlie Hebdo in 2023 and the organization of the Paris Olympic Games in 2024.” Since at least June 2024, the Shahid Kaveh unit has had the ability to scan, access, and control industrial control equipment from Schneider Electric, Siemens, and Rockwell, the French government said in its report. It pins the refrigeration controller hacks on this particular Iranian crew for a couple of reasons. Making the case for attribution First: the infrastructure used to carry out the October supermarket attacks was also used during this timeframe to conduct reconnaissance on Schneider Electric equipment, zeroing in on small- and medium-sized energy and water production units. “The techniques used during these actions are known to have been used by the Shahid Kaveh unit since at least April 2026,” the report says. It also notes that investigators found “traces of Farsi use” in the attack infrastructure. Plus, Iranian media outlet CyberbanNews, which is reportedly linked to the Shahid Kaveh unit, publicized the incidents that occurred late on October 11 and into October 12 extremely quickly: “as early as October 13.” In early November, similar cyberattacks on commercial refrigerators and freezers were reported across Europe , with grocery stores in Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden reporting widespread food losses after miscreants spiked temperatures to as high as 122°F (50°C). Last week, the US federal government urged owners and operators to take security measures to prevent these types of attacks from spreading to America. articles.title: Webex Gets iPhone Duo Support
articles.content: Popular video meeting app Webex was today updated with support for Apple's iPhone Duo . Webex works open or closed, in portrait or landscape mode, and even in a laptop or tent position. When open, the ‌iPhone Duo‌ shows more meeting participants, keeps shared content visible, and gives access to a whiteboard. Multitasking support allows Webex to be used alongside another app with Split View. Webex Mobile Camera Share lets users stream the iPhone's camera in a meeting when the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is open in a laptop position, so participants can view the live camera feed and annotate it. Along with ‌iPhone Duo‌ support, Cisco has added the Webex Notetaker Agent to the iPhone app. It can transcribe and summarize in-person conversations and create action items. Webex can be downloaded from the App Store for free. articles.title: Epic Games Comments On Planned Linux Distribution Support
articles.content: Epic Games says it plans to support its new Linux launcher on as many distributions as possible, specifically naming Fedora, SteamOS, CachyOS and Omarchy. GamingOnLinux's Liam Squires-Hand reports: Speaking to Jake Jones, Communications Director at Epic Games, they said: "Hey Liam! The new Epic Games Launcher is still in Preview and we plan to support as many Linux distributions as possible, including Fedora, SteamOS, Cachy, Omarchy, and more. We're testing and evaluating packaging formats for distribution, and we'll restore AppImage this month." With that in mind, until things settle down, you might see different packaging types appear or disappear until they decide firmly how they plan to support different distributions each with their own different packaging formats. Or, perhaps they might see the Flatpak light and just put it up officially on Flathub. Would make it even easier for SteamOS then too with Flathub, since it would just be a quick pop to Desktop Mode to install it directly in the Discover app. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.author: BeauHD

articles.title: DCU shake-up: James Gunn and Peter Safran out post-merger
articles.content: It's barely been two months since the controversial Paramount and Warner Bros. merger, and we've already got a shockingly unexpected ouster : Co-CEOs of the rebooted DC Universe, James Gunn and Peter Safran, are stepping down from that role despite the Hollywood rumor mill assuming that the duo would be safe. It's unclear whether the pair chose to resign or were forced out, or what will happen to their planned slate of projects beyond 2028's Superman: Man of Tomorrow , which is in post-production. Producer Jeremy Latcham—a protege of Marvel's Kevin Feige who worked with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy among other MCU films—will replace them. Per Gunn and Safran's joint statement : Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision. In that time, we helped restore Superman to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television with Peacemaker , Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface. We’re immensely proud of the team that turned that ambition into something real, including the actors, crews and executives we had the opportunity to collaborate with. We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter. We’re excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in Man of Tomorrow . DCU fans are mourning the news and what it could mean for the franchise. My feelings are mixed. On the one hand, I'm on record that I’ve found the rebooted DC Universe films released thus far to be enjoyable but rather forgettable, even when the positives outweigh the negatives . (I have yet to see Clayface , which debuted to good reviews and a solid box office showing.) But HBO has done right by the DCU: I loved both seasons of Peacemaker; Lanterns is a shining beacon of what is possible when someone is allowed to get really creative within the genre; and I'm very much looking forward to next year's Jimmy Olsen (Skylar Gisondo) series The People v. Gorilla Grodd —described as a “mockumentary crime comedy superhero series.” Read full article Comments
articles.author: Jennifer Ouellette
articles.fingerprint: dcu gunn james merger out peter post safran shake

articles.title: Meta's Muse AI Agent Comes to Apple Watch
articles.content: Meta today updated the Muse app for iOS to add Apple Watch support, which means Muse users can access the proactive AI agent from the watch. The app adds the Muse character to the watch with an option to text it, dictate text to it, or call it. There's also a Muse complication for quick access. Muse is Meta's personal AI agent that can complete tasks for users. It is available as a standalone app and is also built into Instagram, Facebook, and other Meta apps. The yeti-like character Meta designed to represent Muse has become popular, and it is front and center on the Apple Watch. The watch app design is similar to the Muse Charm Meta announced as a companion device in September. articles.title: Anker Launches Eufy Security Cam With Auto-Tracking Light
articles.content: Anker today launched the Eufy TrackLight Cam S1 , which it says is the world's first outdoor security camera with an auto-tracking light for actively deterring intruders. The TrackLight Cam S1 is compatible with Apple Home when using the Anker HomeBase, so it can be used alongside other smart home devices in a HomeKit setup. When a suspicious person is detected, the camera locks on and follows them with a light from up to 12 meters (40 feet) away. The light adjusts with distance, narrowing when someone is far away and broadening as they approach. The camera has 355 degrees of horizontal rotation and can track movement up to 87 degrees per second. An optional tracking deterrence mode activates the light and a 105-decibel siren at the same time, plus there is a red and blue flashing light mode as an additional deterrent. The camera records in 4K with 10x digital zoom and night vision to show strangers in the dark. There is a 120-degree floodlight that works alongside the TrackLight, and dual radars offer 180-degree detection up to 40 feet. A Family List in the app allows the homeowner to set known people, so they get a soft, welcoming light as they approach. The feature detects a known phone's Bluetooth. There's a 15,000mAh battery and a 5.5-watt solar panel for continuous operation, and IP65 dust and water resistance offers protection from the elements. There is no built-in storage, and users will need to add a microSD card or connect to the HomeBase. No subscription is required. Anker also recently launched its Window Camera E10, a 2.5K resolution camera with anti-reflection and 25 degrees of tilt. It's designed to be put in a window, covering a yard, driveway, or entry without needing to be outdoors. The TrackLight Cam S1 can be purchased from Anker or from Amazon.com for $300. The Window Camera E10 is $80 from Anker or from Amazon.com . A bundle with the HomeBase is priced at $500 . Note: MacRumors is an affiliate partner with Anker. When you click a link and make a purchase, we may receive a small payment, which helps us keep the site running. articles.title: The Jensen Huang spy scandal is becoming a White House problem
articles.content: The scandal engulfing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is no longer simply a question of whether one of Silicon Valley’s most powerful men had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. It’s also a question of what the White House knew—and what it might have chosen to overlook. Huang and Nvidia confirmed the relationship Sunday, following a bombshell New York Times report . Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen)—the woman at the center of the revelations—is an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, a major customer of Nvidia chips. U.S. intelligence surveillance reportedly showed that she had been funneling information directly to the Chinese government. What remains unclear is how much sensitive information may have been compromised, what Huang knew about the woman he was seeing, and why U.S. intelligence officials apparently failed to warn him about her suspected ties to Beijing. The answers could prove deeply damaging to both Huang and the White House. “It was pretty clear to a lot of people that [Jensen Huang] would be a target of Chinese intelligence collection,” given his proximity to President Donald Trump and his leadership of a company that is “central to the U.S.-China AI competition,” says Sam Bresnick, a research fellow at Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology. Nvidia’s changing story The admission of the affair also contradicts how Nvidia and Huang himself had previously characterized his ties to Alice Huang. As recently as October 29, company spokesperson John Rizzo described their interactions as routine business dealings, while Huang insisted they were “completely normal and not unusual.” Huang now faces an investigation by Nvidia’s board, although directors said in a statement Sunday that they had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised” and expressed “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.” The board’s investigation may be the least of Huang’s worries. The powerful CEO faces the prospect of bipartisan congressional scrutiny, along with mounting questions about his influence in Washington and his future at Nvidia. The questions Congress wants answered Late last week, three House members—Republicans Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Eric Crawford—sent Huang a letter requesting that he attend a closed-door hearing on the matter in Washington, D.C. Asked by Fast Company on Monday whether Huang intends to attend, Nvidia declined to answer on the record. Next year, the new Democrat-controlled Congress will likely call a number of tech leaders, including Huang, to testify about their dealings with Trump. On Monday, Senator Chris Coons of Delaware called for an investigation into Huang and Nvidia to determine whether national security had been compromised. “We need answers about the relationship between AI billionaires and the Trump administration,” he wrote on X. Coons is poised to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when Democrats take control of Congress in January, giving him considerable power to pursue those answers. There is certainly plenty to investigate. For one, we don’t know whether Alice Huang obtained sensitive information from Jensen Huang and transmitted it to the Chinese government. Bresnick says Huang and his devices may have been in possession of several types of valuable information, including trade secrets about upcoming Nvidia chips, the company’s research strategies, or U.S. government plans to restrict China’s access to advanced AI technology. “Did he provide information to her about the Trump administration’s thinking on AI—U.S.-China competition, export controls, and trade policy more broadly?” Bresnick asks. “Because if [the Chinese] have greater texture on what the administration’s thinking, it’s easier for them to position themselves.” (The White House did not respond to Fast Company ’s request for comment.) articles.title: macOS 27.2.1 Fixes eMudhra Certificate Flaw in Command-Line Tools
articles.content: The macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1 update Apple released today addresses the eMudhra certificate vulnerability, and Apple recommends users update to the latest software. For Macs that run macOS 26 or macOS 15, Apple has released macOS 26.7.3 and macOS 15.8.3. Apple previously blocked the compromised certificates in Safari, Mail, and apps that use Apple frameworks in October to protect most users, but command-line tools like curl and git were still able to accept them. With macOS 27.2.1, command-line tools will no longer accept the certificates. Prior to releasing the macOS 27.2.1 update, Apple offered instructions for those who wanted to protect themselves from the compromised eMudhra certificates when using command-line tools, directing users to manually remove the affected root certificates from their Mac's "/etc/ssl/cert.pem" file. Apple still has those instructions available for users who are unable to update their Macs. The compromised security certificates were issued by certificate authority eMudhra. An investigation launched by Mozilla found the certificates used private key values below 256, making them trivial to recover. Attackers could use the keys to create fraudulent certificates that appeared valid for any website. Apple also fixed the issue in the macOS Golden Gate 27.3 beta , but with the fix also included in macOS 27.2.1, users won't need to wait until December for protection. articles.title: Man who lost $308,000 on sports bets sues Kalshi for offering illegal gambling
articles.content: A man who lost over $308,000 making sports wagers on Kalshi is suing the prediction market for violating the state of Washington's ban on online gambling. He's trying to turn those losses into an overall victory with a lawsuit seeking a payment of over $580,000. Bellevue, Washington, resident Scott Bright's "wagering occurred at a time when it was unlawful in Washington and when the Washington Attorney General had already sued KalshiEX LLC in this Court alleging precisely that," said the gambler's lawsuit filed on September 24 in King County Superior Court. Kalshi has since filed a motion to dismiss the lawsuit. While state attorneys general throughout the US are trying to shut down Kalshi for allegedly violating state gambling laws, Bright's case tests whether unsuccessful gamblers can obtain restitution from the company through individual lawsuits. articles.content: Murat Kurum (left), Turkey’s minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change; and Chris Bowen, Australia's minister for Climate Change and Energy, raise their hands together at the COP31 UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, on November 9th, 2026. | Photo: AFP via Getty Images At this point, reading through the latest splashy pledge to use AI for the good of the environment feels like downing a nonalcoholic beer. Negotiators from more than 190 countries around the world are in Antalya, Turkey, this month for the annual United Nations climate summit, called COP31 (the 31st "Conference of the Parties" that ratified the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change). articles.title: France Accuses Iran of Supermarket Fridge Hacking
articles.content: France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of being behind last month's cyberattacks on fridges and freezers across the country. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression," adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions "at the European level." The BBC reports: The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up, which spoilt fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros. Then last week, dozens of supermarkets across several other European countries were also impacted by a cyber-attack that targeted fridges and freezers. It is not known if the instances are linked. Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people." He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act." France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it," Barrot added. Separately on Monday, the Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as well as his two deputies. Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC. Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime. articles.title: A Sam Altman parody offers an amusing lesson in memory management
articles.content: Sam Altman's recent comments on the Cheeky Pint podcast inspired developer Iain Kay to create a satirical script that allows users to email the OpenAI CEO once per day if more than 10 percent of their system RAM is reported as available. Ram-Altman is described by its creator as a "parody project" launched in response to Altman's viral remarks about RAM in your personal PC. As reported by The Verge , on the October 29 episode recorded with Stripe President John Collison, Altman said, "A lot of people want local inference. And somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now because we are going to have open source models, we’re going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center. But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5 percent of the time." Altman has since explained that his comments were taken out of context and briefly changed his display name to "RAM Altman" on X, which Kay calls on the project GitHub, "objectively excellent and where the project gets its name." articles.title: Awakening ImageCAS: Open Coronary Ostia and Centerlines for CCTA
articles.content: AI-assistance disclosure: I drafted this article with AI assistance, then edited it and fact-checked every number against the paper (arXiv:2611.09714). Anyone who has built a coronary CT angiography (CCTA) workflow knows where the coronary tree starts: at the two ostia, where the left and right coronary arteries leave the aortic root. Curved planar reformation, vessel tracking, branch labeling and stenosis measurement all hang off that point and off the centerline that grows from it. Public data for training a model to find those points has been thin. In arXiv:2611.09714 , Matteo Leccardi and colleagues at Politecnico di Milano, with ETH Zurich and the University of Pavia, fix that for ImageCAS, the largest public coronary segmentation dataset. The project is called Awakening ImageCAS. What they released The release has three parts, all tied to the 1000 CCTA scans of ImageCAS (Guangdong Provincial People’s Hospital, 2012 to 2018): Ostium labels for every scan. A left and a right ostium for all 1000 patients, each stored in world (RAS, mm) and voxel coordinates with the affine matrices, plus a 3D Slicer markup per scan. Rooted centerline graphs. One connected tree per side for 999 of the 1000 patients, grown from the annotated ostia along the official ImageCAS masks. Every node carries position, lumen radius, topological type and side. Files come as networkx-compatible GML, VTK polydata and Slicer markups, with a per-case quality table. Open-weight ostium localizers. Four of six benchmarked 3D models (SwinUNETR-V2, nnResUNet, ResNet50, ResNet101), plus a SwinUNETR-V2 trained at 1.0 mm spacing, with MIT-licensed inference and training code. Before this, the only CCTA data with ostium information were CAT08 and ASOCA, 72 scans in total, where the ostium is only implicit as a centerline start point. CAT08 can no longer be downloaded from an official source. No dedicated ostium localizer had been released with code or weights. How the labels were made The first 500 scans were annotated by three people each, drawn from six trained annotators in rotating groups that reshuffled every 25 images, working in 3D Slicer across axial, coronal and sagittal views. The consensus point is the mean of the three markers, followed by a visual check for gross errors. On these scans an individual annotator sits a mean of 1.45 mm (right) and 1.95 mm (left) from the mean of the other two, so the landmark itself carries a millimeter or two of uncertainty. The second 500 used a human-in-the-loop pass. A SwinUNETR-V2 trained on the first batch plus CAT08 and ASOCA proposed both ostia, and one annotator reviewed every scan. The reviewer moved the point in 88 scans, and the model missed an ostium in 10, which were placed by hand. That took about 5 person-hours, against roughly 144 person-hours for the triple manual annotation of the first batch. The test set comes only from the first, fully manual batch. How the centerlines are grown Instead of thinning the mask into a skeleton, which leaves loops and spurious stubs, the authors resample the mask to 0.5 mm, build a cost that is cheap on the vessel axis and expensive near the wall, and propagate a minimal-cost front from each ostium. The tree then grows by repeatedly tracing the path to the farthest uncovered voxel and keeping it as a branch only if it adds at least 5 mm of new vessel. Because every path comes from the same minimal-path map, the result is a tree by construction. A second pass with a capped wall distance keeps the path centered at bulky bifurcations, and gaps in the mask of up to 10 mm, such as at a severe stenosis, are bridged. The numbers worth knowing On 58 held-out scans (50 ImageCAS, 4 ASOCA, 4 CAT08), SwinUNETR-V2 and nnResUNet found every ostium with no error above 5 mm. Median errors were 0.70 to 0.87 mm per side, below the annotators’ own spread. articles.title: How to Upgrade Kafka Consumers to KIP-848: Faster Rebalances, Safe Commits and Idempotent Writes
articles.content: A Hands-On Java Guide to the Consumer Group Protocol, Server-Side Assignors and a Rolling Migration Without Downtime Photo by Alberto Rodríguez on Unsplash For most of Kafka’s history, every consumer group rebalance has been a small stop-the-world event. One instance restarts, a pod gets rescheduled or you scale from six consumers to eight, and the whole group pauses while the members agree on a new assignment. In a busy system that pause shows up as lag spikes, duplicate processing and on-call pages that say “consumer lag high” at 3 a.m. for no obvious reason. The fix has been production ready since Apache Kafka 4.0: the new consumer group protocol from KIP-848, which moves assignment to the broker and makes rebalances incremental. The catch is that it is still opt-in for the Java client, some familiar configs now throw an exception, and faster rebalances do nothing for you if your commits and writes are not safe. In this guide I walk through how the new protocol works, a production-style Java consumer that commits correctly and writes idempotently, a rolling migration plan and the pitfalls that catch teams out. The Problem Under the classic protocol, the group coordinator on the broker only tracks membership. The actual partition assignment is computed on the client side by one elected group leader. When membership changes, members rejoin through a JoinGroup and SyncGroup round trip, and with the default eager assignors every member gives up all of its partitions until the new assignment arrives. Cooperative rebalancing improved this by revoking only the partitions that move, but it still needs multiple rounds and still depends on every member reaching a global synchronization point. That design creates three recurring problems in production: Group-wide pauses: a single slow or misbehaving member can hold up a rebalance for everyone else. Duplicates: records processed but not committed before a revocation are processed again by the new owner. Complex clients: because the assignment logic lives in every client library, behavior differs between Java, librdkafka and other clients, and upgrades are risky. Core Concepts KIP-848 keeps the consumer API almost the same but changes who does the work. According to the Apache Kafka documentation , the design is fully incremental and no longer relies on a global synchronization barrier. The broker computes the assignment: the group coordinator runs a server-side assignor and sends each member only the partitions it should add or remove. Members that are not affected keep consuming. Everything happens over heartbeats: instead of JoinGroup and SyncGroup, each consumer sends a ConsumerGroupHeartbeat request. The response carries assignment changes, so there is no separate rebalance phase. Two built-in assignors: the broker ships with uniform, the default, and range. A client can request one with group.remote.assignor. Classic RangeAssignor maps to range, while CooperativeStickyAssignor, StickyAssignor and RoundRobinAssignor map to uniform. Timeouts move to the server: the broker configs group.consumer.session.timeout.ms (default 45 seconds) and group.consumer.heartbeat.interval.ms (default 5 seconds) replace the client-side settings. max.poll.interval.ms stays on the client. Static membership still works: setting group.instance.id lets a restarting consumer rejoin with its old identity, and the AWS Big Data Blog notes that short restarts within the session timeout do not trigger a reassignment. The timeline matters for planning. The protocol was early access in 3.7 and became generally available in 4.0. KIP-1274 , now accepted, makes the new protocol the default for KafkaConsumer in Kafka 5.0 and removes classic support from KafkaConsumer in 6.0. Since 4.3, a consumer that still uses the classic protocol logs a message recommending the switch. The latest release, Kafka 4.4.0, shipped on October 22, as summarized in Red Hat’s Kafka monthly digest . Step 1: Check the Brokers The new…

articles.title: OpenBrain: Brain MRI Parcellations Shipped With a Risk Score
articles.content: AI-assistance disclosure: I drafted this article with AI assistance, then edited it and fact-checked every number against the paper (arXiv:2611.05348). When we train a brain parcellation model on pseudo-labels, we run FastSurfer or SynthSeg over a few thousand public T1 scans and get a folder of label maps. Somewhere in that folder are cases where the cortex leaks into the skull or the hippocampus is a scatter of fragments. Nobody opens all of them. In arXiv:2611.05348 , Qizhen Lan, Yu-Chun Hsu, Yuxiang Wei, Lijing Zhu, Zenan Sun, Liang He, Lishan Yu and Xiaoqian Jiang (The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston, Georgia Institute of Technology, University of Houston-Clear Lake and ETH Zurich) release OpenBrain, a set of generated whole-brain parcellations where every case ships with the evidence you need to decide whether to trust it. It was accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets track. What OpenBrain is OpenBrain covers 35,838 T1-weighted scans drawn from 607 OpenNeuro datasets. Each scan is skull-stripped with SynthStrip, resampled to 1 mm isotropic, and parcellated into 110 regions by ModernSurfer, a 3D residual U-Net trained with nnU-Net v2 on FreeSurfer 7.4.1 labels. That is the primary label. Two more models, SwinUNETR and UNETR, parcellate the same scan, and their outputs are released too. They are there as a committee, so you can see where three different architectures disagree. The authors describe these as generated labels and say plainly that they are neither manual annotations nor clinical-grade segmentations. The release is organized as case records: each case folder holds the skull-stripped T1, the brain mask, the three parcellations, and a row in a metadata table with the OpenNeuro source, DOI, license, and whatever age, sex and scanner fields the source dataset published. The seven checks QC-7 is the piece I would copy. It is a panel of seven reference-free checks run on every case. Three look at label geometry: labels outside the brain mask (Q1), region volumes that are unusual for that source dataset (Q2), and pieces of a region far from its main body (Q3). One checks image-label consistency, meaning how much the T1 intensity varies inside each region (Q4). Three measure committee disagreement: overlap between the primary label and the other two models (Q5), voxel-level vote uncertainty (Q6), and differences in region volumes across the three models (Q7). Each raw value is turned into a percentile across the release, flipped where needed so that higher always means riskier. The combined risk score R is the plain mean of the seven percentiles. Sort by R and the lowest quarter becomes HighConf, the middle half Standard, and the top quarter Flagged. The raw values are released alongside the tiers, so if you care more about leakage than about committee agreement, you can reweight and re-threshold without rerunning any model. What it hangs on a scan Open one case and you get a T1, a 110-label map, two alternative label maps, a voxel-wise disagreement picture you can compute from them, and a bar chart of seven percentiles. In the paper’s figure, the lowest-risk case shows clean labels and only thin entropy along region borders. The highest-risk case has labels scattered across a noisy image, entropy filling the brain, and every bar in the red. Testing the risk score The authors froze the checks, the tier cutoffs and the evaluation label set on two development cohorts (IXI and BrainLat) before scoring a manual-label holdout, Mindboggle-101. They then trained nnU-Net on 1,000 lower-risk cases, 1,000 random cases, and 1,000 higher-risk cases. The lower-risk model beat the random one by 3.2 to 3.7 macro Dice points on all three external cohorts. The higher-risk model trailed random by more than 20 points. Where it falls short The labels inherit FreeSurfer conventions. Two of the three validation cohorts use FreeSurfer-derived references, so the largest gains sit inside the same convention…

articles.title: Single-shot and agentic retrieval with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
articles.content: A banking operations employee starts the morning by asking an internal AI assistant which documents are needed to open a business account. The answer is in a single checklist. A few hours later, the same employee asks how those requirements differ across sole proprietorships, LLCs, and partnerships with multiple owners. That answer is spread across several policy guides. One assistant has to handle both questions, quickly and cheaply for the first and thoroughly for the second. Applications need a way to match retrieval effort to each request without building separate systems for simple and complex questions. Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports single-shot Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and retrieval-only requests through AgenticRetrieveStream . With single-shot RAG, the service searches your knowledge bases once and uses a foundation model (FM) to generate an answer from the passages it finds. With retrieval-only requests, the service returns the matching passages without generating an answer, so your application or the user can work with the source text directly. These modes join the existing agentic retrieval, where the service plans and runs multiple searches before answering. You can now use the same API for both of the employee’s questions: single-shot RAG for the checklist lookup and agentic retrieval for the cross-policy comparison. In this post, we explain how the new settings work and when to use each mode. We use an illustrative internal banking policy assistant to show how single-shot RAG handles direct questions and how agentic retrieval supports comparisons across policy documents. We also show how to configure retrieval-only requests when an employee needs to review source passages rather than a generated answer. Key benefits Agentic retrieval helps an assistant answer questions that require more than one search. A foundation model breaks the question into sub-queries, searches the relevant knowledge bases, and evaluates whether the results provide enough information to answer the original question. If it identifies gaps, it can refine the search and retrieve additional evidence, within the configured iteration limit. For application builders, this provides several benefits: Better support for multi-part questions – Targeted searches can find evidence for each part of a question instead of relying on one search to cover everything. In the banking example, the assistant can look up requirements for sole proprietors and LLCs separately before comparing them. Follow-up searches when information is missing – The planner can use what it finds to decide what to search for next. It can also retrieve a full document when a passage doesn’t provide enough context, helping address gaps that a single retrieval might leave unresolved. Answers with supporting evidence – When response generation is enabled, the service combines retrieved information into an answer with citations. Trace events show the planning and retrieval steps, helping developers inspect how the answer was produced. Less custom orchestration – The service manages the planning, retrieval, evaluation, and response-generation workflow through one API. Applications don’t need to implement their own loop to coordinate these steps. These agentic capabilities remain valuable for complex questions. For straightforward lookups, applications also need a way to retrieve and answer without additional planning. The expanded maxAgentIteration range closes that gap. With one parameter, you can choose one of three modes for each request: Retrieval-only returns passages without generating an answer. Single-shot RAG retrieves once and generates an answer, with no planning rounds. Agentic retrieval plans and runs multiple searches for complex questions. Single-shot RAG uses one foundation model call to generate the answer, which can reduce latency and model usage compared with agentic retrieval. Retrieval-only requests make no foundation model calls. You…

articles.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS
articles.content: Today, we are announcing the availability of Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Claude Fable 5.2 is Anthropic’s most capable generally available model for technical work that raises the bar in coding and the sciences. Claude Mythos 5.2 is available through Anthropic’s verification programs for advanced work in cyber security and life sciences. In this post, we cover what’s new in both models, why Fable 5.2 matters for your technical workloads, and how to get started building with the model on Amazon Bedrock. Why Claude Fable 5.2 Fable 5.2 raises the bar on the hardest problems in coding, math, and science. It takes on ambiguous, multi-step work, verifies its own output, and can run unattended for hours to days. It interprets prompts, iterates, catches its own errors, and optimizes as it goes. In Anthropic’s alignment testing, Mythos 5.2 hallucinates less, completes tasks more reliably, surfaces important information more consistently, and self-reports issues more honestly than Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1. Anthropic expects Fable 5.2 to behave similarly. If a cyber security query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 4.8, and if a biology query is declined, you can retry it on Opus 5. On Amazon Bedrock, the retry is your code’s job, not an automatic switch. If the declined request hit the prompt cache, the refusal also includes a fallback credit token. Send that token with the retry and it’s billed as cache reads, so you don’t pay to write the same cache twice. Check the documentation for more information on fallback credit. For authorized work in cyber security and life sciences, Claude Mythos 5.2 is available through Anthropic’s verification programs . Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 use cases Where Fable 5.2 fits: Agentic coding across large, multi-repository codebases. Long-running agents for coordinating many subagents on multi-day work. Scientific research from new analytical methods to formal mathematical proofs. Financial analysis for quantitative research and forecasting. Design for 3D, hardware, and motion for generating environments, components, and simulations in code. Mythos 5.2 covers two high-risk domains, available only through the verification programs noted earlier: Cyber security , for security engineering, red teaming, and penetration testing. Life sciences research , especially biomolecular design and research synthesis. Data retention and Enterprise Frontier Safeguards Anthropic designates Claude Fable 5.2 as a Covered Model . By default, its use requires retention for up to 30 days and human safety review. On Amazon Bedrock, Amazon personnel perform the review within the AWS boundary. Set the aws_review data retention mode on your account or project before you invoke the model. See Amazon Bedrock data retention for more details. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), built in collaboration with AWS, combines the privacy of zero data retention (ZDR) with the latest safeguards for detecting misuse. EFS is available now. A version that keeps your data in a bucket and under keys you control is expected to follow, and it has not launched yet. Until it does, eligible customers can use Fable 5.2 with zero data retention through June 30, 2027. Getting started with Claude Fable 5.2 on Amazon Bedrock To try Fable 5.2, open the Amazon Bedrock console , choose Test , Playground , and select Fable 5.2 as the model. From there, you can run a prompt directly against it. Programmatically, you can call the model with the Anthropic Messages API against bedrock-runtime (through the Anthropic SDK). You can also stay on the Invoke and Converse APIs on bedrock-runtime through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDK . Prerequisites To follow along with the code examples in this post, you need the following: An active AWS account with Amazon Bedrock access. AWS CLI installed and configured with appropriate credentials. Python 3.9 or later. Boto3 (AWS SDK for…

articles.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
articles.content: Today, we’re announcing that NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. You can deploy it with a few steps in SageMaker Studio or with a few lines of the SageMaker Python SDK. Super VL is the vision-language model (VLM) in the NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 family. It accepts images, video, and text as input and generates text. The model pairs a 120B-parameter hybrid Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language backbone with 12B active parameters and a C-RADIO vision encoder. It supports context lengths of up to 1 million tokens and includes a built-in Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) head that supports speculative decoding. You can configure reasoning per request. NVIDIA built Super VL for document intelligence, GUI understanding for computer-use agents, video question answering, and multimodal agentic applications. JumpStart offers two variants: NVFP4, quantized from BF16 with quantization-aware distillation for optimized inference, and the BF16 full-precision reference weights. In this post, we walk through the model’s capabilities and the JumpStart deployment configurations. We then show the measured inference performance and demonstrate text, image, and video inference. Model overview Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a 120B-parameter model with 12B active parameters per token. It combines a hybrid language backbone with a dedicated vision encoder. Language backbone : 88 layers that interleave Mamba-2 and MoE layers (512 routed experts, 22 active per token) with 8 attention layers, plus a shared MTP head. The backbone is initialized from Nemotron 3 Super Base and distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra Base. Vision encoder : A C-RADIO vision encoder encodes images and sampled video frames, and a vision-language connector maps them into the language backbone’s embedding space. The encoder and connector stay in BF16 in both variants. Training : The model first goes through continued pre-training, long-context and software-engineering mid-training, and vision-language training. It then goes through two-stage multimodal supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on vision, reasoning, code, tool, chat, safety, and long-context data. Next come reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiable rewards and human feedback in NeMo RL and NeMo Gym, multi-teacher on-policy distillation, and a final stage that further trains the MTP head. The NVFP4 checkpoint is produced from BF16 with NVIDIA Model Optimizer and quantization-aware distillation. It keeps the vision encoder, connector, Mamba convolutions, and embeddings in BF16 and the MoE router in FP32. It runs with 4-bit weights and activations (W4A4) on Blackwell GPUs. The following table compares the specifications of the two variants available in JumpStart. Specification NVFP4 BF16 Parameters 120B total, 12B active 120B total, 12B active Intended for Optimized inference (latency and throughput) Full-precision reference weights for customization: SFT, RL, distillation, domain adaptation, and custom quantization Inputs / output Image, video, text / text Image, video, text / text Context length Up to 1M tokens (JumpStart serving configurations use 520 to 15,600 tokens) Same Checkpoint size About 75 GB About 249 GB JumpStart instances ml.g7.24xlarge (default), ml.g7.48xlarge ml.p5en.48xlarge Speculative decoding Built-in MTP head. Not enabled in the JumpStart serving configuration Same LoRA adapter serving No No Languages English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Spanish, Chinese Same Reasoning On by default. Configurable with enable_thinking Same Outputs Tool calling, JSON schema output, configurable reasoning Same License OpenMDW License Agreement, version 1.1 Same Key use cases Super VL is aimed at agentic workloads that must see and read. It targets vision-language agents that combine reasoning, coding, tool use, document understanding, and video understanding. articles.title: How to watch Rivals: Fury vs Joshua for free, online and from anywhere
articles.content: Rivals: Fury v Joshua is the perfect hors d'oeuvre to what is quite simply the biggest fight in British boxing history. On December 11, 2026, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will finally end decades of verbal sparring by actually facing off in the ring.
